ideas.title: Price the opening ask near the median, not above it
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py set the opening ask for each item at about the market median (lamp ~105-110, chair ~190, bookshelf ~275) instead of the upper quartile, and set the target at or just under the median. Keep the reserve + 5 floor in code.
ideas.evidence: Our shop has 20 deals from 27 visits (1.1% share), but the top shops with medians near the market (corner-store {'bookshelf': 290, 'chair': 195, 'lamp': 110}, outseop {'chair': 182, 'bookshelf': 262, 'lamp': 100}) win 15-29%. Our reviews include 'Could not agree on a price' (2*, twice) and 'No agreement within my budget'. Our buyer also skips shops above the upper quartile, so a high ask means we may be filtered out before negotiating.
ideas.expected: More visits convert to deals. Deal count and share should rise, with a slightly lower average price per deal. Stars should improve as fewer 'could not agree' reviews appear.
ideas.risk: Lower margin per deal. If the medians are already close to our current asks, the change will have little effect.
ideas.honest: Only changes the asking price, which is a real price we will charge. No false claims, and the reserve floor is unchanged.
ideas.test: Run for 2-3 hours against the previous 15-minute config. Compare conversion (deals/visits), 'no agreement' review share, and mean margin over reserve.

ideas.title: Open with a concrete, honest ask and a quick first counter
ideas.what: Make the Llama reply always state the item, our actual current ask and a plain 'send your offer as a number'. Have the code generate the first counter by conceding toward the buyer's offer immediately (e.g. a counter within ~5% of the buyer's first offer when it is above the floor), and make the 'Deal: item at X' line a fixed template, with no free-form LLM text on prices.
ideas.evidence: Winners use short templated lines: corner-store 'Counteroffer: 306 / 275 / Deal: bookshelf at 267', 11im 'Counteroffer: 105 / 107 / Deal: lamp at 103', dragonash '260 is too low. Counteroffer: 270.' Reviews reward speed: 11im '5*: deal after 2 offers', ggari-shop '2 counters'. Others show 5 offers until the end, and 11im has a 2* review for an API failure. Our 8B model may add latency or errors.
ideas.expected: Fewer rounds per deal, fewer errors and timeouts, and a higher conversion rate. Stars should rise slightly from 'quick and fair' reviews.
ideas.risk: Conceding faster can leave some money on the table with buyers who would have paid more.
ideas.honest: Every number quoted is a real counter we would accept. Nothing is claimed about other buyers or deadlines.
ideas.test: Log rounds-to-deal, error rate and conversion before and after. Check the review text for 'quick', 'fair' and 'error'.
flags: ties a reward to reviews or stars

ideas.title: Open higher on the first offer to cut the round count
ideas.what: Our buyer currently ends up paying near the ask anyway (dragonash bookshelf: asks [282,272,269,268], offers [262,266,267,268]). Instead, start the first offer at ~92-94% of the shop's median (not the 255-262 we use now) and raise by small steps. Stay within budget and the 1.1 x upper-quartile cap.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer pays 266-268 on dragonash bookshelves every time while 'it sold at 260 to others'. Offers of 255-262 never move dragonash below ~266, so the low opening gains nothing and costs 4-5 rounds. We also had 5 walks, such as 11im lamp budget 90 (walked) and 11im chair budget 160 (walked), where the budget is below every price.
ideas.expected: Fewer offers per trade with about the same final price. Better success rate where the gap is small. It is mainly a speed and reliability gain.
ideas.risk: A higher first offer might cost 1-3 units on shops that would have conceded more. It does not help when the budget is under every price.
ideas.honest: Offers are real and within budget. Only the opening level changes.
ideas.test: A/B the opening ratio over the next 40 trades. Compare average paid/budget (currently 86.8%) and offers per deal.

ideas.title: Prefer shops whose public price level fits our budget before negotiating
ideas.what: Before the first offer, rank candidate shops by their published item median from the ledger. If the budget is below the shop's median for that item, skip it up front and go to a cheaper shop, such as outseop (lamp 100, chair 182), ggari-shop (lamp 100, chair 180) or kimauve (bookshelf 260, chair 180). This avoids three-offer walks.

These budgets are below the medians of those shops (11im lamp 104, chair 186; ggari-shop chair 180). Cheaper shops with deals at the budget exist in the table.
ideas.expected: Fewer no-deal trades (5 of 40), and some wasted rounds avoided. A modest rise in success rate.
ideas.risk: A low-budget order may have no affordable shop at all. Median data can be stale, so some cheaper shops may be skipped incorrectly.
ideas.honest: Only uses public ledger data and our own budget, and says nothing untrue about the shops.
ideas.test: Count walks per 40 trades, compared to the current 5. Check that reviews written remain factual.

ideas.title: Quick close near market median on first counter
ideas.what: Change the concession rule so that when a buyer's offer is within ~5% of the quartile median for that item (e.g. chair >=180, lamp >=100, bookshelf >=262), the shop accepts or counters at a price just above reserve+5 instead of conceding only 40% of the gap. Cap rounds at 2 so the deal closes quickly, with a signed receipt.
ideas.evidence: Our shop has 20 deals out of 28 visits (share 1.1%) and 3 of 8 sampled reviews are 'Could not agree on a price' (2*). Top shops close fast: dragonash 'Deal: bookshelf at 266' after 2 offers, ggari-shop 'Fair deal at 180 after 2 counters', and 11im sells lamps at 103-105 with counters of 105/107. Our buyer closes dragonash bookshelves at 266-268 after counters of 4-5 steps.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed negotiations, so more deals per visit (maybe 71% to 80%+) and fewer 2* 'could not agree' reviews, lifting stars toward 4.0. Slightly lower average price, offset by volume.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks on buyers who would have paid more; the acceptance band may be set too low if the market drifts.
ideas.honest: Prices stay at or above reserve+5, no false claims are made, and the buyer is simply offered a fair market-level price sooner.
ideas.test: A/B by alternating the concession rule per 15-min meta_shop cycle; compare deals/visits, share of 'could not agree' reviews, and average margin over ~100 visits each.

ideas.title: Open the ask nearer the market median (no padding)
ideas.what: Set opening ask per item to roughly the median plus ~3% (chair ~195, lamp ~108, bookshelf ~283) rather than the current quartile-based opening, and keep the target at the median. State the ask plainly without invented 'was' prices.
ideas.evidence: outseop-26510122 got a 3* review: 'The shop opened at 202, above the 199.2 market average... so its opening ask was padded.' Meanwhile ggari-shop opens chair at 204 and lands 184, while kimauve, with medians 105/180/260 close to market, converts 126/156 visits (81%). Our visit-to-deal rate is 71%.
ideas.expected: Better conversion and fewer reviews calling the ask padded; modestly higher stars and share; average price drops a few percent.
ideas.risk: Leaves money on the table with buyers who accept the opening ask; if market medians fall we may chase the price down.
ideas.honest: Opening is a real price we'd honor, with no fake anchor; it is just closer to the true market level.
ideas.test: Change the opening-ask knob in meta_shop.py for half of the cycles; track review text mentioning padding or 'could not agree', deal rate, and average sale price.

ideas.title: Retry and fast-fail guard so rate-limited visits are not lost
ideas.what: Wrap the Llama call in the Worker with a short backoff and retry. If the model still fails, fall back to a rule-based reply: ask price, then accept at or above target, with no LLM needed. Log each failure with a counter.
ideas.evidence: Two 1* reviews of our shop read 'Failed to trade: RuntimeError: Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn ... 429 Rate limit reached'. Our deal rate is 132/241 visits (55%), while 11im converts 2108/2719 (78%) and lee-sungsoo 1825/2378 (77%).
ideas.expected: Each saved visit is a deal and each avoided 1* review lifts the average stars. Even a few points of conversion should raise share.
ideas.risk: The fallback replies are less flexible than the LLM. The 429 may come from the buyer's harness, not from us, so only part of the loss is fixable.
ideas.honest: It affects reliability only. All deals still go through signed receipts, with no false claims.
ideas.test: Count the 429 and timeout reviews and the conversion rate (deals/visits) before and after. Compare with the 55% baseline over the next 100 visits.

ideas.title: Put the deal terms in the first reply: price, receipt and one-word close

ideas.expected: Higher conversion, since buyers with a budget at or above the ask close on turn 1. Fewer turns also means fewer chances for LLM errors. Expect a few points of deal rate.
ideas.risk: A clear ask may leave money on the table from buyers who would have paid more. Low-budget buyers may still walk.
ideas.honest: The terms are true: the price is the real ask and the receipt is really signed. It states no scarcity and no fake 'was' price.
ideas.test: A/B the template against the current opening, split by visit parity. Compare deal rate, average turns per deal and price paid as a share of budget.

ideas.title: Walk-away rescue: escalate to a second shop at the going median instead of ending the visit

Look up the going-price median for the item in the last 3 hours and re-pick the cheapest shop that is signed, has stars of at least 4.3 and is not above the upper quartile. Make sure the budget covers the median first. Skip the item if it does not.

ideas.what: Our reviews show 2-3 star losses where the seller 'clung' to 105/185/265 or 'stayed at 265' while buyers offered 230 and budgets of 90/160. Going medians are lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260. Lower the opening ask to about the market median plus 5 and set target at the median (never below reserve + 5). Counter once at the median when a buyer's offer is within ~10% of it, instead of conceding 40% of the gap in small steps.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: '2* seller clung to 105 ... budget was 90', '2* seller clung to 185 ... budget 160', '2* seller stayed at 265'. Top shops 11im, lee-sungsoo, JangSeongWoong all have medians at 100/180/260 and win 20%+ share with 4.4+ stars.

ideas.title: Fix 429/timeout failures with faster, cheaper responses
ideas.what: Two 1-star reviews are caused by 'Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn: Error 429 rate limit'. Reduce LLM calls per turn: handle price parsing and counteroffers in code, and use Llama 8B only for the short text. Add a deterministic fallback reply (a rule-based counter or accept) when the model call fails or exceeds a time limit, and cache the responses for repeat prompts.

ideas.risk: Rule-based text is less persuasive; the 429 may originate on the buyer's side and not be fixable by us.

ideas.risk: No shop may sell under budget, so some trades still fail; chasing cheap shops may land on shops with weaker reviews or no signed receipts.

ideas.title: Open at the market floor on items where rivals hold the floor
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py set opening ask equal to target equal to the observed middle-half low (bookshelf 260, chair 180, lamp 100) instead of a higher opening ask with concessions. Keep the code rule of never selling below reserve + 5. Keep the opening line short and factual: 'Asking 260, signed receipt, no added fees.'
ideas.evidence: Top shops lee-sungsoo (21.2% share) and nocha12 open and hold at 260 and say 'one reply accepting it closes the deal'. 11im sells at 260-263. Our reviews: 2* 'Shop refused to budge from 265 despite three reasonable offers' and 2* 'Could not agree on a price', while going median is 260.
ideas.expected: More closed deals per visit (our 271 deals / 441 visits = 61% vs 11im 79%, lee-sungsoo 78%), fewer 2* no-agreement reviews, higher share; per-deal price drops about 2%.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks if reserve is near 260. Buyers with high budgets pay less than they would have.
ideas.honest: The ask is a real price we actually charge, with no false 'was' price. We never go below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: A/B by item across 15-minute meta_shop cycles for 24h: floor-open vs current. Compare deals/visit, stars and revenue per visit.

ideas.title: Reply with a single final price once the buyer is within a few units of it
ideas.what: Add to the shop code: if the buyer's offer is within about 2% of the target, answer with one clear 'Deal at X' or 'Final price X, reply accept' instead of another 40%-of-gap counter. Counters stay at X (no endless rounds). Cap rounds at about 3.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo's reviews show 'deal after 8 offers' and its replies are one-line 'lowest price, one reply accepting it closes the deal'; our 2* review 'Could not agree on a price' and the 429 failures show long negotiations get lost. Buyers' own review: 'nocha12 ... 3 offers until the end'.
ideas.expected: Fewer abandoned negotiations, fewer timeouts under rate limits, deals/visit up toward 75-80%, small star gain.
ideas.risk: Some buyers who would have paid more are closed early; a firm line may cost a few units.
ideas.honest: States a true final price and honors it. The shop never pressures with fake deadlines or scarcity.
ideas.test: Compare mean offers per deal, deals/visit and 1-2* share before and after the change for 24h.

ideas.title: Show receipt number with a real, honored repeat-visit discount
ideas.what: Include the signed receipt number in the deal message and tell the buyer that quoting it on the next visit gives X% off, applied through our existing loyalty code table. Do not ask for or condition anything on reviews in the same sentence.
ideas.evidence: 11im (21.7% share) says 'Receipt No. ...: mention it on your next visit for an extra 3% off' in every deal message. We have loyalty tiers and one-time codes, but our codes are not surfaced as a simple receipt-number mention.
ideas.expected: More repeat visits and a higher share of loyalty-tier orders; share growth over several hours. Cost about 3% on repeat deals.
ideas.risk: Discount may cut into margin below reserve + 5; buyers may not remember to mention it.
ideas.honest: A genuine, honored discount tied to a true receipt; no review conditioning. Dropping the 'please leave a review' line from the same message keeps the discount fully separate from reviews.
ideas.test: Count visits that quote a receipt number, repeat-buyer rate, and margin on those deals over 48h versus the control period.
flags: ties a reward to reviews or stars

ideas.title: Open near the market floor and walk less on tight budgets
ideas.what: In the buyer, start the first offer at the lower middle-half price for the item (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) when the budget is at or above it. When the budget is below every price, skip the 3 offers and move directly to the next shop whose ask is lowest in the ledger, rather than walking from the same shop. Do not retry the same shop twice in a row where it walked.
ideas.evidence: Our last 40 trades: 11 no-deals, mostly 'walked' at lee-sungsoo (chair budget 160, bookshelf budget 230 twice) and dragonash chair 160, while the going median chair is 180 and bookshelf 260; those budgets are below every price. Also the buyer paid 86.1% of budget on average.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted turns and fewer rate-limit failures; no-deal rate down from 27% as budgets below the median are matched to shops that actually concede (e.g. corner-store, yms979, leeuichann closed at 100 on a 105 budget).
ideas.risk: Budgets under the market price may have no seller at all; then walking is correct and the number of no-deals will not fall.
ideas.honest: We offer only within our true budget and never reveal a false budget; skipping shops is not deception.
ideas.test: Track no-deal rate and mean paid/budget over the next 40 trades against the previous 40, split by budget below or above the median.
